✦ Hi, I'm Xiaojing

I'm a phonetician and PhD researcher at the Cambridge Phonetics Laboratory, University of Cambridge. My research measures how voices shimmer and shift: from the tones of Jin Chinese to the subtle breathiness hiding in everyday English speech.

Before Cambridge, I studied at Wake Forest University, earning a B.S. in Mathematical Statistics & Linguistics in 2024 — where I first discovered that language and mathematics could grow side by side in the same field.

I'm currently working on two main projects: a frame-level voice quality classifier that teaches machines to hear what phoneticians hear, and the tones of Huojia Jin Chinese, a dialect with secrets buried deep in its mountain terrain.

📄 Publications

Interspeech 2026

The Role of Phonation Type in Chinese Jin Tones: A Study Using Acoustic Metrics

Du, X., Nolan, F., & Post, B.

Interspeech 2026

Tonal convergence in Huoji (Jin Chinese) compresses f0 space, so T1 and T5 overlap when the checked tone's glottal constriction weakens late-vowel f0. Comparing Praat, YIN, and REAPER trackers, we show that f0-only measures keep T5 nearest T1, but adding HNR05 and H1*–H2* separates them — phonation-sensitive measures complement f0 when periodicity is locally unreliable.
▾ tap to expand
Conference Talk · 2026

Segmental vs. Suprasegmental Glottalization in a Jin Chinese Dialect: Phonetic Pathways of Tone and Phonation

Du, X., Nolan, F., & Post, B.

International Conference on Phonetic Variation 2026, University of Granada

Examines how glottalization operates at both the segment and the suprasegmental (tone) level in a Jin Chinese dialect, tracing the phonetic pathways linking tone and phonation.
▾ tap to expand
In Preparation · 2025

Tonal Perception and the Huojia Minimal Pair: Listener Sensitivity to Phonation Cues

Du, X., Post, B., & Nolan, F.

ICPhS 2027 (in preparation)

A perception experiment using resynthesised Huojia Jin minimal pairs to isolate which acoustic dimensions (F0, VQ, duration) listeners use to distinguish tones. Directly tests Lu et al.'s theoretical claims with Cambridge participants.

🔭 Research & Events

Ongoing Projects

Voice Quality and Tone in Jin Chinese

University of Cambridge · 2025 – Present
  • Investigating phonation type in Jin Chinese tones, contributing speech-science evidence from an under-studied Sinitic variety.
  • Analysing F0, duration, HNR, H1–H2, CPP, and frame-level voice quality measures alongside SSL-derived probes.
In Progress

Interpretable Voice Quality Labelling

University of Cambridge · Interdisciplinary · 2026 – Present
  • Voice quality terminology is fragmented across linguistics, clinical, and engineering fields — this project works toward a shared, reusable frame-level voice quality detector.
  • Funded by the Cambridge Language Sciences Incubator Fund ("Hearing Every Voice: Interpretable Voice Quality Labelling for Inclusive AI").
In Progress

Huoji Tone Perception — Further Data Collection

University of Cambridge · Fieldwork: Henan, China · 2026 – Present
  • Collecting further perception data on the Huoji dialect to test whether listeners rely on F0, phonation, or both to distinguish the T1–T5 tone contrast, replicating and extending Lu et al.'s methodology.
  • Aims toward a complete production-and-perception picture of the Huoji dialect, alongside the ICPhS 2027 paper in preparation.
In Progress
